stem: A client has chronic lower-leg swelling, aching and heaviness, varicose veins, and skin changes that worsen after prolonged standing and improve with elevation. Which condition best matches this pattern?

options.A: Chronic venous insufficiency with impaired venous return and venous hypertension.
options.B: Peripheral arterial disease presenting primarily as exertional claudication that improves with rest.
options.C: Acute deep vein thrombosis as the usual explanation for years of bilateral varicosities and chronic stasis skin changes.
options.D: A normal age-related change that needs no vascular assessment when edema improves with elevation.

rationale: The 2026 StatPearls entry describes chronic venous insufficiency as impaired venous flow with venous hypertension and common manifestations including dependent edema, discomfort/heaviness, varicose veins, and progressive skin changes. Symptoms may improve with rest and leg elevation and are not characteristically tied to exercise. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize the characteristic chronic venous-insufficiency pattern of dependent edema, heaviness/aching, varicosities and stasis skin changes that improve with elevation.
source_locator: Continuing Education Activity; History and Physical > Clinical Features: impaired venous blood flow/venous hypertension; edema, varicose veins, pain/heaviness and skin changes; symptoms may improve with rest and leg elevation.
source_claim_supported: Chronic venous insufficiency causes venous hypertension and commonly presents with dependent edema, aching/heaviness, varicose veins and skin changes that may improve with elevation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14: manage clients with acute/chronic physical-health conditions and recognize pathophysiology and clinical manifestations.

source_original.rationale: Chronic venous insufficiency commonly causes lower-extremity edema, aching/heaviness, varicosities and skin changes. Symptoms often worsen with prolonged standing and improve with rest or elevation.

correction_summary: Retained key A and the venous-insufficiency pattern, verified the newly updated 2026 StatPearls entry, tightened the DVT distractor to distinguish acute disease from chronic stasis changes, and reduced difficulty to medium.

audit_findings.exact_locator: Continuing Education Activity and History/Physical Clinical Features
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately integrates chronic edema, heaviness, varicosities, stasis skin changes and elevation response.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because arterial claudication is exercise-related and does not explain the chronic venous skin/varicosity pattern.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because acute DVT does not ordinarily explain years of bilateral varicosities/stasis changes.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because these are vascular disease findings, not normal aging.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A explains the full chronic pattern.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are vascular/clinical interpretations of the same findings.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read current StatPearls, all choices, rationale, objective and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
